primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: A full-thickness paraumbilical abdominal-wall defect, usually to the right of the umbilicus, allows bowel to protrude directly into amniotic fluid without a covering membrane.
vignette: A newborn has loops of edematous bowel protruding through an abdominal-wall opening just to the right of a normally inserted umbilical cord. No membrane covers the exposed intestine.
distractor_notes: Omphalocele protrudes through the umbilical ring and is covered by a sac.
An umbilical hernia is skin-covered and does not expose bowel directly to amniotic fluid.
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia places abdominal viscera in the thorax rather than through a paraumbilical wall defect.
Bladder exstrophy exposes bladder mucosa in the lower abdominal wall rather than free bowel loops.
key_expl: A right-sided paraumbilical defect with uncovered bowel is the defining gross pattern of gastroschisis.
objective: Differentiate gastroschisis from omphalocele using defect location and presence or absence of a covering membrane.

sources.title: About Gastroschisis
sources.support: CDC describes bowel protruding through a hole beside the umbilicus, commonly on the right, without a protective sac.

sources.title: Gastroschisis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes gastroschisis as an abdominal-wall defect with bowel outside the abdomen and distinguishes it from membrane-covered omphalocele.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Failure of normal diaphragm development permits abdominal viscera to occupy the fetal thorax, compressing the developing lung and producing pulmonary hypoplasia.
vignette: A term newborn develops severe respiratory distress immediately after birth. The abdomen appears scaphoid, breath sounds are markedly decreased on the left, and imaging shows bowel loops occupying the left hemithorax.
lead: Which developmental consequence most directly explains this newborn's respiratory failure?
correct: Pulmonary hypoplasia from intrathoracic compression of the developing lung
distractors: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from vitamin K deficiency
distractor_notes: Maternal antibodies do not cause the characteristic thoracic bowel and scaphoid abdomen pattern.
Tracheoesophageal fistula causes feeding-related choking and aspiration rather than bowel within the hemithorax.
Pulmonary arterial thrombosis does not explain congenital bowel herniation through the diaphragm.
Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding, not developmental displacement of abdominal organs into the chest.
key_expl: Abdominal viscera in the fetal thorax restrict lung growth; the resulting pulmonary hypoplasia is the central cause of severe neonatal respiratory compromise in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
objective: Explain respiratory failure in congenital diaphragmatic hernia through impaired fetal lung development.
clues: scaphoid abdomen and immediate respiratory distress

sources.title: About Diaphragmatic Hernia
sources.support: CDC explains that abdominal organs can enter the chest and prevent complete lung development.

sources.title: Diaphragmatic hernia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes congenital diaphragmatic hernia with underdeveloped lung tissue and severe neonatal respiratory distress.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Dysfunctional B-cell maturation and antibody production cause low immunoglobulin levels, classically including IgG with IgA and/or IgM deficiency, leading to recurrent sinopulmonary infection.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has recurrent bacterial sinusitis and pneumonia. Serum IgG and IgA are markedly decreased, T-cell count is normal, and HIV testing is negative. She had no major infections in early childhood.
lead: Which immune abnormality most directly explains this patient's recurrent infections?
correct: Impaired differentiation/function of B cells with inadequate antibody production
distractors: Failure of beta-2 integrin-mediated leukocyte adhesion
Complete absence of thymic T-cell development
distractor_notes: Defective oxidative burst causes chronic granulomatous disease rather than multi-isotype hypogammaglobulinemia.
Beta-2 integrin failure causes leukocyte adhesion deficiency with neutrophilia and impaired tissue migration.
Terminal complement deficiency predisposes particularly to Neisseria infection without the characteristic low IgG/IgA pattern.
Profound T-cell developmental failure causes severe combined immunodeficiency, usually presenting much earlier.
key_expl: CVID is characterized by defective B-cell maturation/function with reduced antibody production, especially low IgG with low IgA and/or IgM.
objective: Explain recurrent sinopulmonary infection in CVID through impaired humoral antibody production.

sources.title: Common variable immune deficiency
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes recurrent lung/sinus infections and deficiency of IgG with IgA and sometimes IgM due to dysfunctional B-cell antibody production.

sources.title: TNFRSF13B gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes TACI function in B-cell survival, maturation, and antibody production and its association with a subset of CVID.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: LYST variants disrupt lysosomal trafficking, producing abnormally large lysosomes and related granules in immune and pigment cells, causing recurrent infections, partial oculocutaneous albinism, and bleeding tendency.
vignette: A 4-year-old child has recurrent pyogenic infections, easy bruising, silvery-gray hair, and light skin. Peripheral blood smear shows giant cytoplasmic granules in granulocytes.
lead: Which intracellular process is most directly impaired in this disorder?
correct: Lysosomal trafficking and regulation of lysosome-related organelles
distractors: Assembly of the terminal complement complex
distractor_notes: Oxidative-burst failure causes chronic granulomatous disease and does not explain giant lysosomal granules with partial albinism.
Beta-2 integrin deficiency causes leukocyte adhesion deficiency rather than abnormal giant lysosomes and pigment dilution.
Class-switch defects cause hyper-IgM syndromes.
Terminal complement defects predispose to Neisseria infections without the characteristic granule and pigmentation findings.
key_expl: LYST encodes a lysosomal-trafficking regulator; pathogenic variants produce enlarged dysfunctional lysosomes and related organelles in immune and pigment cells.
objective: Link Chediak-Higashi syndrome to defective LYST-dependent lysosomal trafficking.
clues: giant granulocyte granules with recurrent infection

sources.title: Chediak-Higashi syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes recurrent infections, oculocutaneous albinism, bleeding, enlarged lysosomes, and LYST-related lysosomal trafficking dysfunction.

sources.title: LYST gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes the lysosomal trafficking regulator and the abnormal lysosomal structure/function caused by LYST variants.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ITGB2 variants disrupt the beta-2 integrin subunit, preventing firm leukocyte adhesion to endothelium and subsequent transmigration into infected tissue.
vignette: A 3-month-old infant has recurrent bacterial skin infections, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, delayed separation of the umbilical cord, and almost no pus at infected sites.
lead: Which leukocyte step is primarily defective?
correct: Firm adhesion to vascular endothelium before transmigration
distractors: Chemotaxis toward bacterial products after tissue entry
Antibody class switching in germinal centers
distractor_notes: Selectin-mediated rolling precedes beta-2-integrin-dependent firm adhesion and is not the defining defect in LAD1.
Chemotaxis can occur once leukocytes reach tissues; the major LAD1 block is failure to adhere and exit the bloodstream.
Oxidative burst failure causes chronic granulomatous disease, not delayed cord separation with neutrophilia and absent pus.
Class switching is a B-cell process and does not explain failure of neutrophils to enter tissue.
key_expl: LAD1 results from beta-2 integrin deficiency, so leukocytes cannot firmly adhere to endothelium and cross the vessel wall.
objective: Link delayed cord separation, absent pus, and neutrophilia to beta-2-integrin-dependent adhesion failure.

sources.title: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes delayed cord separation, absent pus, recurrent infection, ITGB2 variants, and failure of leukocyte adhesion/transmigration.

sources.title: ITGB2 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes beta-2 integrins binding endothelium and enabling leukocyte passage across the vessel wall.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ELANE-associated severe congenital neutropenia can result from misfolded neutrophil elastase accumulation that damages neutrophil precursors and causes profound neutropenia beginning in infancy.
vignette: An infant has recurrent bacterial pneumonia and skin infections beginning in the first months of life. Absolute neutrophil count is persistently 180/mm3. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic ELANE variant.
lead: Which cellular mechanism best explains the neutropenia?
correct: Toxic accumulation of misfolded neutrophil elastase leading to neutrophil death
distractors: Failure of B-cell maturation in the bone marrow
Loss of beta-2 integrin-mediated neutrophil adhesion
Defective NADPH oxidase activity in mature neutrophils
Failure of terminal complement complex formation
distractor_notes: B-cell maturation failure causes agammaglobulinemia, not isolated profound neutropenia.
Beta-2 integrin deficiency causes LAD1 with circulating neutrophilia rather than severe neutropenia.
NADPH oxidase deficiency impairs killing but does not reduce neutrophil number to this degree.
Terminal complement deficiency predisposes to Neisseria infections without severe neutropenia.
key_expl: A common ELANE-associated mechanism in severe congenital neutropenia is misfolded neutrophil elastase accumulation with injury and death of neutrophil-lineage cells.
objective: Explain ELANE-associated severe congenital neutropenia through toxic protein misfolding and neutrophil loss.

sources.title: Severe congenital neutropenia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes congenital profound neutropenia, recurrent infections, and ELANE-associated unstable/misfolded proteins causing neutrophil death.

sources.title: ELANE gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes misfolded neutrophil elastase accumulation and neutrophil death in severe congenital neutropenia.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: ELANE variants can cause recurrent approximately 21-day cycles of neutropenia because affected neutrophils have shortened survival and marrow neutrophil supply periodically falls.
vignette: A 9-year-old child has mouth ulcers, fever, gingivitis, and bacterial infections every 3 weeks. Between episodes she is well. Serial blood counts show severe neutropenia during symptomatic periods and normal counts between them.
distractor_notes: Severe congenital neutropenia causes persistent rather than regularly recurring neutropenia.
CVID causes antibody deficiency and recurrent sinopulmonary infections rather than periodic ANC nadirs every ~21 days.
LAD1 causes persistent neutrophilic leukocytosis with impaired tissue migration, not cyclic neutropenia.
Familial HLH causes systemic hyperinflammation with fever, cytopenias, and organ involvement rather than predictable neutrophil cycles.
key_expl: Regular symptomatic neutropenic episodes separated by normal neutrophil counts are characteristic of cyclic neutropenia.
objective: Recognize cyclic neutropenia from recurrent approximately 3-week neutrophil nadirs with oral inflammation and infection.

sources.title: Cyclic neutropenia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes recurrent neutropenia about every 21 days with mouth ulcers, gingivitis, fever, and infection.

sources.title: ELANE gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes ELANE variants, shortened neutrophil lifespan, and the cyclic pattern of neutropenia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: PRF1 or related cytotoxic-granule pathway defects impair cytotoxic lymphocyte control of activated immune cells, producing persistent immune activation and systemic hyperinflammation.
vignette: A 10-month-old infant develops persistent fever, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, very high ferritin, and hepatitis after a viral illness. A sibling died in infancy with a similar illness. Genetic testing identifies a PRF1 variant.
lead: Which immune function is most directly impaired?
correct: Cytotoxic lymphocyte perforin-mediated elimination of activated target cells
distractor_notes: Neutrophil rolling is mediated primarily by selectins and does not explain familial systemic hyperinflammation.
Class-switch defects produce hyper-IgM phenotypes rather than HLH.
C3 deficiency causes recurrent pyogenic infection and immune-complex disease, not the characteristic familial hyperinflammatory syndrome.
IgE cross-linking mediates immediate hypersensitivity, not failure to terminate cytotoxic immune responses.
key_expl: PRF1 encodes perforin; impaired cytotoxic lymphocyte killing prevents appropriate down-regulation of activated immune responses and contributes to familial HLH.
objective: Link familial HLH to defective perforin/cytotoxic-lymphocyte control of immune activation.

sources.title: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes familial HLH as exaggerated immune activation due to defects in genes that help eliminate unneeded activated lymphocytes, commonly PRF1 or UNC13D.

sources.title: PRF1 gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes perforin in cytotoxic lymphocyte killing and PRF1 variants associated with familial HLH.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: SH2D1A-related loss of SAP disrupts lymphocyte signaling and immune control, creating severe susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus with fulminant HLH, dysgammaglobulinemia, or lymphoma.
vignette: A previously healthy 7-year-old boy develops Epstein-Barr virus infection followed by persistent fever, hepatosplenomegaly, hepatitis, and pancytopenia. A maternal uncle died after infectious mononucleosis in childhood.
lead: Which lymphocyte signaling defect most directly underlies this patient's susceptibility to severe EBV-associated disease?
correct: Loss of SAP-dependent signaling from SH2D1A dysfunction
distractor_notes: NADPH oxidase deficiency causes chronic granulomatous disease.
C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency causes hereditary angioedema.
ADA deficiency causes a form of severe combined immunodeficiency.
Beta-2 integrin deficiency causes leukocyte adhesion deficiency.
key_expl: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease type 1 is caused by SH2D1A variants that eliminate or impair SAP, disrupting lymphocyte signaling and immune control of EBV.
objective: Explain severe EBV-associated disease in X-linked lymphoproliferative disease through SH2D1A/SAP dysfunction.
clues: maternal male relative with similar death

sources.title: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes severe EBV-associated HLH, dysgammaglobulinemia, lymphoma, and X-linked disease.

sources.title: SH2D1A gene
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes SAP-dependent lymphocyte signaling and SH2D1A variants causing X-linked lymphoproliferative disease.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is an aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly presents with a rapidly enlarging nodal or extranodal mass and may produce constitutional B symptoms.
vignette: A 71-year-old man has a rapidly enlarging painless cervical mass, drenching night sweats, fever, and weight loss. Excisional biopsy shows sheets of large atypical CD20-positive lymphoid cells.
distractor_notes: Follicular lymphoma is typically indolent and composed of follicular architecture rather than sheets of rapidly proliferating large B cells.
CLL usually presents with persistent lymphocytosis and small mature-appearing lymphocytes.
Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells in an appropriate background rather than diffuse large CD20-positive B-cell sheets.
Waldenström macroglobulinemia is an indolent lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma characterized by IgM paraproteinemia.
key_expl: A rapidly growing mass with B symptoms and diffuse sheets of large CD20-positive B cells is characteristic of DLBCL.
objective: Recognize diffuse large B-cell lymphoma from its aggressive tempo and large mature B-cell morphology.
clues: large CD20-positive cells with B symptoms

sources.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
sources.support: NCI defines DLBCL as a fast-growing B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with rapidly growing tumors and possible B symptoms.

sources.title: Aggressive B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Treatment
sources.support: NCI describes DLBCL as the most common NHL subtype and notes rapidly enlarging masses and systemic B symptoms.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Hairy cell leukemia is an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm with characteristic immunophenotype and a strong association with activating BRAF V600E.
vignette: A 58-year-old man has fatigue, recurrent infections, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and no significant lymphadenopathy. Peripheral smear shows lymphocytes with fine cytoplasmic projections. Flow cytometry is positive for CD11c, CD25, and CD103.
lead: Which molecular alteration is most strongly associated with the classic form of this leukemia?
distractor_notes: BCR::ABL1 is characteristic of chronic myeloid leukemia and some ALL.
JAK2 V617F is common in several myeloproliferative neoplasms such as polycythemia vera.
PML::RARA defines acute promyelocytic leukemia.
MYC rearrangement is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.
key_expl: Classic hairy cell leukemia is strongly associated with the activating BRAF V600E mutation.
objective: Associate classic hairy cell leukemia with BRAF V600E.

sources.title: Hairy Cell Leukemia Treatment
sources.support: NCI describes hairy cell leukemia, splenomegaly, cytopenias, characteristic immunophenotype, and frequent BRAF V600E.

sources.title: Hairy cell leukemia
sources.support: NCI defines hairy cell leukemia as a rare indolent B-cell leukemia with abnormal lymphocytes having hair-like projections.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Waldenström macroglobulinemia is an indolent lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma that secretes IgM; high circulating macroglobulin can produce hyperviscosity symptoms.
vignette: A 69-year-old man has fatigue, blurred vision, headaches, epistaxis, and splenomegaly. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a large monoclonal IgM spike.
lead: Which circulating immunoglobulin is primarily responsible for this patient's hyperviscosity syndrome?
distractor_notes: IgA is not the defining monoclonal macroglobulin in Waldenström macroglobulinemia.
IgE mediates immediate hypersensitivity and is not the characteristic paraprotein.
IgG4 is not the defining secreted immunoglobulin of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.
IgD can occur in rare plasma-cell disorders but does not define Waldenström macroglobulinemia.
key_expl: Waldenström macroglobulinemia is an IgM-secreting lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma; the large pentameric IgM protein can markedly increase serum viscosity.
objective: Explain hyperviscosity in Waldenström macroglobulinemia through monoclonal IgM production.

sources.title: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
sources.support: NCI defines Waldenström macroglobulinemia as an indolent lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with abnormal IgM and possible hepatosplenomegaly/lymphadenopathy.

sources.title: Macroglobulinemia
sources.support: NCI explains that high levels of large serum proteins can make blood too viscous to flow normally through small vessels.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Myelodysplastic syndromes are clonal marrow neoplasms in which immature blood cells fail to mature effectively, producing one or more peripheral cytopenias and a risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia.
vignette: A 74-year-old man has progressive fatigue and easy bruising. Hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL, platelets are 72,000/mm3, and leukocytes are 2,900/mm3. Bone marrow is hypercellular with dysplastic myeloid and erythroid precursors and 6% blasts.
lead: Which bone-marrow process most directly explains this patient's peripheral cytopenias?
correct: Ineffective maturation of clonal hematopoietic precursors
distractors: Complete absence of hematopoietic stem cells
Peripheral immune destruction limited to platelets
Iron depletion causing isolated erythroid failure
Acute replacement of marrow by >50% lymphoblasts
distractor_notes: Aplastic anemia is characterized by markedly hypocellular marrow rather than hypercellular dysplastic hematopoiesis.
Immune thrombocytopenia causes isolated platelet destruction, not multilineage cytopenias with dysplastic marrow.
Iron deficiency primarily causes anemia and does not explain multilineage dysplasia.
A high lymphoblast burden would indicate acute lymphoblastic leukemia rather than low-blast myelodysplasia.
key_expl: MDS produces clonal, dysplastic, ineffective hematopoiesis: marrow may be cellular or hypercellular while mature circulating cells are reduced because precursors fail to mature effectively.
objective: Explain cytopenias in myelodysplastic syndrome through ineffective clonal hematopoiesis.

sources.title: Myelodysplastic Syndromes Treatment
sources.support: NCI describes MDS as cancers in which immature marrow cells fail to mature into healthy blood cells and notes risk of progression to AML.

sources.title: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms—Patient Version
sources.support: NCI identifies myelodysplastic syndromes as diseases of blood cells and bone marrow and links to current expert-reviewed MDS information.
